title: audit-log-exporter: wire S3 export sink + retention config for Private installer
author: Priya Shah
body: Summary: Wire the audit-log-exporter Helm chart and Private installer terraform module to support S3 export sinks and per-tenant retention policies. This change hooks up the installer outputs (KMS ARNs, VPC endpoints, bucket names) into the audit-log-exporter chart values, adds retention configuration and lifecycle rules, and exposes a toggle to enable cross-account export for enterprise customers. Motivation: Customers running Redwood Private require automated, auditable export of audit logs to customer-owned S3 buckets with retention/Lifecycle controls to meet compliance (SOC2, PCI) and for long term storage. Previous manual post-install steps were error-prone for installers and upgrades; this PR automates wiring and makes upgrades idempotent. Changes included: - Terraform: redwood-private-installer module: add outputs for audit_log_bucket_name, audit_log_bucket_arn, audit_log_kms_key_arn, audit_log_vpc_endpoint_id, and an optional trusted_account_id for cross-account exports. Add aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration resource to manage retention days and transition rules when provided. - Helm: redwood-helm-charts/audit-log-exporter: add values.audit.sink.s3.* values (bucket, region, kmsKeyArn, vpcEndpointId, crossAccountRoleArn), retentionDays, lifecycleRules, and templates to render bucket policy-only when cross-account enabled. Add pre-install hook to validate presence of required secrets (kms key ARN). - Installer wiring: redwood-private-installer/helm/wiring: inject outputs from terraform into HelmRelease values.yaml, conditionally enable cross-account role creation when trusted_account_id is supplied. - Upgrade path: add migration job manifest that reconciles existing buckets and applies lifecycle policies during upgrade to avoid data loss; job runs once during chart upgrade and is guarded by a Helm hook with timeout. - Tests & CI: add unit tests for values rendering and a small integration test in perf-canary to deploy a local minio-backed S3 and verify exporter can write events and retention lifecycle gets applied. Checklist: - [x] Terraform outputs and lifecycle resources implemented - [x] Helm values and templates updated - [x] Installer wiring injecting outputs - [x] Upgrade migration job implemented and tested - [x] Unit and integration tests added - [x] Docs updated (installer quickstart note) Commits (summary): - Add S3 retention lifecycle to installer module (Priya) - Expose audit-log outputs for Helm wiring (Priya) - Helm chart: add s3 sink values and templates (Arjun) - Add migration job for upgrade path (Maya) - Tests: add unit tests and perf-canary integration (Priya) Files changed (high level): - terraform/modules/private-installer/main.tf (added s3 lifecycle, outputs) - terraform/modules/private-installer/outputs.tf (new outputs) - helm-charts/audit-log-exporter/values.schema.json (added audit.sink.s3 schema) - helm-charts/audit-log-exporter/templates/s3-sink.yaml (new template) - helm-charts/audit-log-exporter/templates/migration-job.yaml (upgrade migration job) - installer/helm/wiring/values-generator.go (wiring logic) - perf-canary/integration/audit-exporter-s3-test.yaml (integration) - docs/private/audit-log-exporter.md (installer docs) Review thread (high-level): - Arjun Patel: requested changes to bucket policy generation for least privilege, asked to add unit test for policy rendering. - Priya Shah: addressed comments, updated policy generation and added unit test. - Maya Li: reviewed migration job, asked for additional logging and failure handling (added exponential backoff + requeue). - Noah Kim: flagged that cross-account role creation must be optional and requires approver step in enterprise installer; added tenant flag and docs note. CI status: See ci_checks. Merge: Squash and merge after final approvals. Notes: kept values and template changes backward compatible; retentionDays defaults to 365 (configurable).

release_notes: Add automated wiring for audit-log S3 export sinks in Private installer, including retention lifecycle management and upgrade migration job. Backwards compatible; retentionDays defaults to 365. Admins should review cross-account export docs before enabling.
